label: Uneasy standoff
summary: 41 — the pressure campaign hardens into a stated aim of regime collapse. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised the 'toughest sanctions in history' to bring Iran's government down and asked China to join; Beijing refused, saying sanctions settle nothing. Brent held above $93 for a second straight weekly rise while Wall Street sold off on climbing Treasury yields. North Korea fired ballistic missiles as the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills wound down. In Hong Kong, Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung were convicted of subversion for organising Tiananmen vigils. The Panama Canal reversed itself and will cap transits at 34 a day from 4 September as El Nino drought looms; 800 fled a wildfire in western Spain. Against that: the Taliban freed two detained UN staff, 70,000 Ebola doses are heading to DR Congo, and a pancreatic cancer drug raised immune responses in high-risk patients. No editorial adjustment.
